justification: One new documentation file. No code, no query, no served value. The branch predates the per-branch QA report requirement, which is why CI reported the report absent rather than the change being unsafe.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The branch touches anything other than the single documentation file it claims to add. A docs-only claim is falsifiable by the diff itself, and that is the only claim being made.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Verified today: the diff against origin/main is exactly 1 file, 72 insertions, 0 deletions. Adding any second path would make the diff list more than that one file.

pre_impl.existing_data: None read or written. The file records a decision rule for solar A-F grading, written before the investigation that would apply it.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The branch looked abandoned during the audit. It is not - it is a pre-commitment record, and its value depends entirely on having been written BEFORE the analysis. Landing it late preserves the commit date in git history, which is the part that matters; rewriting it now would destroy the property it exists to have.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds a file. Nothing is modified or removed, so nothing can regress. Note the branch is three weeks old, but its diff is one file - merging it cannot revert any doc changed on main since. Rebased onto main 2026-08-26 so it runs against current tests and the per-branch gate. Rebase preserves author dates, so the 2026-08-07 pre-commitment evidence is intact; only the commit hash moved.

break_it.scenario: Grade thresholds are chosen after seeing which side of them the answer falls on.
break_it.what_happens: The grade stops being a measurement and becomes a presentation choice, while still reading as a measurement. Nothing in the output would reveal it.
break_it.how: This document fixes the rule in git before the analysis exists. Its commit date is the evidence, which is why it is landed rather than rewritten.
break_it.repro: git log -1 --format=%aI e1f7e8f7 returns 2026-08-07T20:28:05+10:00 — the AUTHOR date survived the rebase onto main, which is the date that matters. The commit hash changed because the branch was rebased to pick up current tooling; the evidence did not.
